title: Chapter 2 Quiz 3
description: More families of algorithms and the problems they solve.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Which kind of algorithm is designed to put data in **ascending or descending order**?
questions.explanation: Sorting algorithms arrange data in a given order. Watch out: a searching algorithm only finds an element, it does not reorder anything.

questions.question: Match each family of algorithms to how it works.
right: Arranges data in a specific order
Finds the position of an element in a data set
Makes the best local choice at each step
Splits a problem into sub-problems, solves them and combines the results
questions.explanation: Sorting orders, searching locates, greedy chooses the best immediate option, divide and conquer splits and combines.

questions.question: Merge sort and quick sort are best described by which design idea?
questions.explanation: They split the data into smaller parts, solve each part and combine the results. Watch out: they are also sorting algorithms, but the question asks about the design idea.

questions.question: Autocomplete and looking up records in a database use mainly…
questions.explanation: Searching algorithms find a given element quickly in a data set.

questions.question: Scheduling and shortest-path problems are typical uses of…
questions.explanation: Optimization problems like these use the best immediate choice at each step. Watch out: sorting may help, but it is not what these problems are about.

questions.question: A greedy algorithm makes the locally best choice at each step.
questions.explanation: That is the definition of a greedy algorithm.

questions.question: Which of these are **sorting** algorithms?
questions.explanation: Selection, bubble and merge sort order data. Watch out: binary search works best on sorted data, but it searches and does not sort.

questions.assertion: Sorting data is often done to prepare it for searching.
questions.reason: Ordered data lets a search algorithm find an element more efficiently.
questions.explanation: Both are true, and the reason explains the assertion: sorted data can be searched much faster.

questions.question: Put the steps of a divide and conquer algorithm in order.
questions.explanation: Divide, solve, then combine: that gives the name of the method.
